titles: How to Maximize Your Social Security Benefit
Claiming Social Security at 62 Could Cost Your Spouse
Waiting Until 70 Isn't a Social Security Strategy
description: Most people spend 30 or 40 years paying into Social Security, then about 30 minutes deciding how to claim it.
Aaron Christopherson, CFP®, walks through four things to understand before you file — and why the decision matters most for married couples.
• Why Social Security uses 35 years of earnings, and what zeros do to that average
• Why claiming at 62 and waiting until 70 are both strategies, not defaults
• How spousal benefits work, including on a former spouse's record
• Why the surviving spouse may be the biggest factor in the whole decision
